transcript: They say good things come in small packages and that is the case with Danger and Opportunity by Ken Urban. This piece of microtheater takes place in a living-room-sized site-specific venue in the East Village. An audience of about 40 people lurks along the perimeter of the room witnessing two men in a sexually stale marriage connecting with one of their exes who happens to be a woman. Things escalate quickly for the three of them, and as the title suggests, where there is opportunity, there is danger. I thought this was a fascinating character study and reflection on relationships, brought to life by the incredibly naturalistic direction by Jack Serio and three performers who have effortless chemistry with each other. Given the intimate nature of the venue, you really get to take in the minute details of their facial expressions and body language, and there's a level of almost nonperformative honesty in the delivery of the script that you can't truly capture in a larger space. It's hard to describe but the synergy of the script, the direction, and the performances in this specific venue leaves an impression that's greater than the sum of its parts — everything is intentional, no matter how seemingly small. With that, another program for my collection.
